To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
structural features of retaining glycosytransferases favor an orthogonal mechanism.

the binding of metal-nucelotide-sugar between inverting and retaiing enzymes is conformational and requires the donor to occupy two different orienations, and that the structures of retaining enzymes lack appropriate enzymatic residues for a dissociative mechanism and show the acceptor and donor in close proximity.

the binding modes of the metal-nucleotide-donor sugar are unique for inverting and retaining glycosyl transferases and that this structural difference is the key to understanding the different reaction mechanisms used by the two types of transferases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of the glycosyltransfer enzymes, and the structural and chemical factors that influence their catalytic efficiency.
the mechanism of retaining glycosidases and glycosyltransfer-ases.
the mechanism of glycosyl transfer reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the available data support a front-side attack mechanism for the retaining glycosyl transfer reaction.
the structural data available to date support a front-side attack mechanism for retaining enzymes.
the available structural data support an orthogonal mechanism for retaining glycosyltransferses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structural and kinetic data are consistent with an orthoester mechanism, which is a special case of an orthogonal mechanism.
the structures of glycosyl transferases, and the enzymes that catalyze the reverse reaction (glycosidases), support a front-side mechanism for retaining glycosyl transferase enzymes.
the structural features of retaining glycosidases are not compatible with a dissociative mechanism, while those of retaining glycosytransferases are consistent with an in-line (orthogonal) mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structures of glycosyl transfer enzymes can now be used to predict the stereochemical outcome of the reaction.

the structural features of glycosyl transferases are more consistent with the orthogonal mechanism than a dissociative mechanism, but that the structural features are also consistent with a double displacement (SN1-like) mechanism.
the mechanism of retaining glycosylation is not the result of a random, or even a concerted, process but instead the result of a geometrically constrained reaction.
